newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi lops eight points off base rate to 27 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malawi lops eight points off base rate to 27 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Malawi said on Thursday it was cutting its base lending rate to 27 percent from 35 percent, effectively immediately.
A statement from the central bank said the decision followed a careful review of the underlying developments in the economy that pointed to a further improvement.

"Most notable among these developments has been the continuous deceleration in the rate of inflation now forecast to be less than eight percent, on annualised basis, by end December 1996," the statement said.
The foreign exchange reserves position had remained strong and was projected to improve in the months ahead with the receipt of donor support for the balance of payments, the statement said.
In September, the Reserve Bank cut its lending rate to 35 percent from 45 percent.
Commercial banks had already lowered their lending rates to 29 percent from 37 percent at the start of November.
